newsitem.title: CHINA: Head of Chinese garrison in Hong Kong visits Tung.
newsitem.headline: Head of Chinese garrison in Hong Kong visits Tung.

text.p: The head of Chinese troops stationed in Hong Kong on Friday made his first known visit to the territory's new leader Tung Chee-hwa after the ex-British colony returned to Chinese rule, the government said. Major-General Liu Zhenwu, Commander of the Hong Kong Garrison of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA), paid a "courtesy call" on Tung at Government House where former colonial governors resided, a government statement said.
China retook Hong Kong at midnight on Monday, concluding 156 years of British colonial rule. Tung has been picked by a Beijing-supervised caucus to govern the post-handover region.

Beijing has sent PLA troops to Hong Kong, saying it is a symbol of sovereignty. In his visit accompanied by the garrison's senior officers, Liu repeated the force's pledge to abide strictly by Hong Kong law, and Chinese law on the troops.
Liu also briefed Tung on the garrison. The government described their talk as "long and cordial".
"Tung said Hong Kong was very fortunate to have a group of such fine and highly disciplined military personnel stationed here," the statement said.
At dawn on Tuesday, the first day of resumed Chinese rule, the main body of China's 4,000 troops in Hong Kong entered the territory in armoured cars, trucks and by ship.
The entry of the main contingent brought the size of the Chinese force here to nearly 5,000 after 509 troops entered late on Monday to reinforce 200 advance soldiers who had come earlier.
Pro-democracy activists regarded the arrival of the PLA forces, and particularly armoured cars, as a provocative reminder of the 1989 Tiananmen Square massacre in Beijing.
